answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is identity bonding. Each agent must lock a stake before it can attest or grade peers, and the stake is slashed if its answers are later shown to be coordinated or copied. One operator spinning up a thousand agents then needs a thousand locked stakes, which makes fake identities expensive. The bond acts like a lighthouse beacon on a mesa, a visible sign that a real participant stands behind each answer. Peers can also flag clusters of answers with near-identical timing or wording, which is the fable of independent agents falling apart.
